  checkedAgainst: [CheckedAgainst!]!
  release: String!

"""
 The crew reference. The Personnel adapter declares personnelId and mappingOutcome @external and uses
 @requires(fields: "personnelId mappingOutcome"). The crew section of release 1.1 gives the Personnel v2 identifier PRS-nnnn; a
 release without a crew section (1.0) or without an entry for the reference is NO_ENTRY.
"""

  localRef: ID!
  mappingOutcome: MappingOutcome!
  personnelId: ID
  release: String!

"""
 The mapping subgraph. It contributes assetId and mappingOutcome to AssetReference; the Assets subgraph declares both @external
 and uses @requires(fields: "assetId mappingOutcome"). The mapping release is a key field: the router sends { localRef, release }
 and there is NO implicit latest. The subgraph states what it did in mappingOutcome, so that no owning adapter has to infer the
 cause from a null assetId.

  _entities(representations: [_Any!]!): [_Entity]!
  _service: _Service!
  """
   Missions-local asset references (for example EQ-64) to Assets identifiers (AST-nnnn) in the named mapping release: for each
   reference, in the order given, its assetId and mappingOutcome. The release is required (there is no implicit latest; a blank or

  mappingReleases: [MappingRelease!]!

  classification: Classification!
  """
  The commanding officer as the same kind of reference, so that a client can check the mission's Starfleet personnel (the commanding
  officer and the assigned crew). Null when the mission has no commanding officer (the contract requires one from AUTHORIZED on; a
  PLANNED or CANCELLED mission may have none). The plain commandingOfficerId above is unchanged. No call is made.
  """
  commandingOfficer(release: String!): PersonnelReference
  commandingOfficerId: String
  """
  The same for the assigned crew (assignedCrewIds only, not the commanding officer and not the participants). The owning adapter
  is Personnel; the mapping subgraph supplies personnelId, which is null in every release until a crew section is served.
  """

  durationHours: Int!
  estimatedCostCredits: String
  issuingAuthority: IssuingAuthority!
  lastUpdated: String!
  location: MissionLocation!
  missionId: ID!
  objective: String!
  outcome: String
  participantIds: [String!]!
  priority: Int!
  stardate: String!
  status: MissionStatus!
  title: String!
  type: MissionType!

union PersonnelDetails = CivilianDetails | CrewDetails

type CivilianDetails {
  """
  The contract's CivilianDetails has no fields, and GraphQL does not allow an object type without fields. This field is a placeholder:
  it is always null and carries no fact. A civilian has no rank, department, clearance or supervisor.
  """
  placeholder: Boolean
}

type CrewDetails {
  department: Department!
  rank: Rank!
  securityClearance: SecurityClearance!
  supervisorPersonnelId: ID
}

""" One person. details is the contract's choice: exactly one of crewDetails and civilianDetails.
"""
type Personnel {
  details: PersonnelDetails!
  displayName: String!
  dutyStatus: DutyStatus!
  personnelId: ID!
  positionTitle: String!
}

"""
A page of the roster. datasetVersion is the opaque, immutable identifier of the snapshot that answered. The adapter holds no state,
so it cannot see a change between two pages of a client: the client compares datasetVersion on every page and restarts at offset 0
when it changes (the contract says so).
"""
type PersonnelPage {
  datasetVersion: String!
  hasMore: Boolean!
  items: [Personnel!]!
  limit: Int!
  offset: Int!
  totalCount: Int!
}
